functional_goal: Qualify, deploy, roll back, soak, measure, and finally retire the Python Re-CTM production runtime without dual authority, data loss, or an unbounded performance claim.

final_release_requalification.reason: Synchronize final production-authority and completed-milestone status without making the binary claim knowledge of host Python-installation state.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: Invoking the pinned cargo executable without the pinned toolchain bin on PATH could not find the cargo-fmt subcommand.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Used the existing exact project rustup toolchain environment rather than weakening formatting or lint gates.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The initial process sampler split /proc/*/stat on spaces; process names containing spaces caused the whole resource sample to be discarded and RSS was falsely recorded as zero.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Rejected the evidence, replaced child discovery with /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children, added real RSS/thread/fd sampling, and reran all seven Python and Rust repetitions.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first short soak mixed normal allocator warm-up with steady-state memory growth, making the whole-run RSS slope too close to the threshold to support a leak conclusion.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Extended the soak to sixty seconds, measured a tail window after fifteen seconds, added absolute RSS/tail-growth/fd/thread/child limits, and reran it.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first candidate report attempted to hash a temporary rollback wheel after its temporary directory had already been removed.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Captured wheel SHA-256 and size while the artifact existed and retained only non-sensitive immutable facts in the candidate report.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: Two full MTM-007 target reruns observed a public tunnel URL but the external metadata endpoint was transiently unavailable while all local and owned-child checks passed.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Kept the same acceptance condition, confirmed the exact standalone public-metadata path, and reran the complete target suite until the real edge metadata and owned cleanup both passed.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first live restart inherited no operator password for three sessions, so the generated OAuth key was written into owner-only background logs even though public evidence remained redacted.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Rejected the first live evidence, atomically rolled back to Python, rebuilt equivalent Python sessions, removed the first deployment root, generated replacement keys into dedicated mode-0600 files, restarted every session with RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD set, and reran the complete live cutover/rollback/recutover. The final logs contain only the configured-externally marker.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first retirement run installed the immutable wheel and served valid OAuth metadata, but the harness incorrectly required exit code zero after deliberately terminating the restored Python server with SIGTERM; the evidence was therefore rejected.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Kept the successful metadata requirement, accepted only bounded normal shutdown results (zero, SIGTERM, or SIGINT), continued to reject forced kills, and reran the idempotent retirement flow.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The retirement report passed all seventeen checks, but direct execution of the independent validator could not import the scripts package from its script-directory sys.path.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Added the same script/module import fallback used by the earlier target validators, changed no acceptance condition, invalidated the evidence hash, and reran both retirement and independent validation successfully.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: README preparation exposed that the renamed mtm executable still consumed RE_CTM_* environment variables and defaulted to ~/.re-ctm, so co-installed MTM and Re-CTM could still share configuration and runtime state despite distinct command names.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Moved MTM runtime configuration exclusively to MTM_*, changed the default runtime-data root to ~/.mtm, retained Re-CTM at RE_CTM_*/~/.re-ctm, forked the previously shared runtime state under a stopped-session boundary, and added architecture/governance checks that reject namespace regression.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.stage: MTM-007 resource reference after environment separation
recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first post-namespace MTM-007 target rerun gave the Python reference MTM_* variables, so its OAuth operator password was absent and the reference authorization correctly failed with HTTP 403.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Made the target harness choose MTM_* only for Rust and RE_CTM_* only for the frozen Python reference, then reran the full twelve-check target suite successfully.

evidence: Rust 0.3.0 workspace formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, Rust tests, governance tests, and graph validators pass.
The deployment manager has atomic-selector, rollback, recutover, mode, and fail-closed identity tests.
The final local gate includes the independent seventeen-check retirement validator and authority inventory.
All MTM-002 through MTM-007 frozen differentials remain exact.
The final release-info contract identifies mtm 0.3.0, Rust implementation, no Python runtime, 24 public tools, 11 hidden aliases, state schema 2 and workflow protocol 2.
The existing eighteen-checkpoint full-composition Python-Rust differential still has zero mismatches.
Candidate cutover tests use disposable command links, state roots, databases and workspaces.
The command link selects exactly one release atomically and manifests are owner-only.
Retirement fails unless Rust is active, the rollback wheel hash matches, and no Python-tool-root process remains.
The retired Python selector kind is converted to a wheel record so legacy symlink rollback fails closed rather than creating a broken production command.
The obsolete re-ctm-native-helper symlink was removed only after proving it resolved inside the retired Python tool root.
All MTM-003 through MTM-007 real target reports are fresh after the Rust 0.3.0 release changes.
A real Re-CTM 0.3.0 wheel was built, restored with uv, executed, and used in both temporary and live rollback drills.

Four live Python serve/TUI sessions and their owned descendants stopped cleanly, the user command selected Rust, live rollback selected Python, recutover selected Rust, and all four sessions restarted on the exact recorded Rust release.
Generated operator keys are owner-only secret files and no raw key is present in the final background logs or evidence.

After deleting the installed Python tool root, the hash-recorded wheel was restored into an isolated uv tool root, reported re-ctm 0.3.0, served real OAuth metadata, and shut down with a bounded signal.
All four live sessions were upgraded to the final release SHA-256 7142cf77775552533fc6472f46391989cc1d5d3ed12d1bdf08c48b7d7ae70728.
The command-separated sixty-second Rust soak completed 169990 requests with zero errors and 29 stateful start/cancel cycles.
Tail RSS growth was 928 KiB, fd/thread growth was zero, no child process remained, and shutdown was graceful.
Seven repetitions per runtime and 5600 measured requests per runtime used the same authenticated local OAuth/MCP workload with eight clients.
Final public-release measurement observed Rust/Python median throughput ratio 2.225839; p95 latency ratio 0.505386; peak RSS ratio 0.669716.
Final conservative bootstrap ratios were 2.205282 throughput, 0.52023 p95 latency, and 0.674448 RSS, all beyond predefined thresholds.
A6.claim_scope: Authenticated loopback OAuth/MCP ping, tools/list, server_info, read_file, and check_exec_environment under eight concurrent clients only.

post_completion_command_namespace_correc.reason: The original final command name re-ctm would collide when MTM and Re-CTM are installed together.
post_completion_command_namespace_correc.first_attempt_failure: The first namespace cutover used uv's sandbox HOME defaults, so re-ctm was not linked into /home/lk/.local/bin after the four MTM sessions had stopped.
post_completion_command_namespace_correc.repair: Pinned UV_TOOL_DIR and UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR to the real user installation roots, retained the already-installed mtm release, restored Re-CTM independently, recovered the four MTM sessions, and generated one replacement mode-0600 operator key because the original environment-only key disappeared with its stopped process.
post_completion_command_namespace_correc.alias_policy: MTM provides no re-ctm compatibility alias; Re-CTM provides no mtm alias.

manual_pending: Other operating systems, deployment users, reverse proxies, and site-local CAS/LaTeX layouts require their own release evidence.
Publishing the internal mtm-* crates to a public registry is optional and is not required by the accepted single-binary deployment.
rollback: MTM rollback must remain inside the mtm command namespace; Re-CTM restoration remains inside the re-ctm namespace. Never repoint either command to the other project's executable. State schema 2 and workflow protocol 2 remain compatible; no database rewrite is required.
